The EBG-backed folded slot antenna achieves a front-to-back ratio exceeding 15 dB at around 9.7 GHz.
The antenna bandwidth with EBG substrate is approximately 7.5% at 10-dB return loss.
The antenna gain is measured at about 3.7 ± 0.2 dB, with an estimated efficiency between 80% and 90%.
The EBG substrate consists of a two-dimensional square lattice of dielectric rods with lattice constant 1.2 cm and rod size 4.8 mm, dielectric constant 10.2.
The EBG substrate creates an omnidirectional stopband between 7.5 GHz and 10 GHz for TM polarization.
Simulations used a full-wave integral equation/method of moments code and HFSS finite-element method.
The folded slot antenna length is 18.0 mm and width 2.0 mm for the EBG-backed design.
A reference folded slot antenna without EBG substrate shows significant pattern distortion and low front-to-back ratio (~0 dB).
Parasitic parallel-plate waveguide modes cause energy leakage and pattern dips of 7–8 dB in reference antennas.
The EBG substrate reflects parallel-plate TEM modes, preventing energy leakage through finite ground edges.
Supporting dielectric material left on the back plate (10–20% of substrate height) does not significantly affect antenna performance.
The EBG cavity formed is frequency-dependent and tunable by adding more EBG layers.
The two-dimensional EBG crystal avoids parasitic surface states that degrade efficiency in three-dimensional EBGs.
The antenna was fabricated on RT/Duroid substrates with dielectric constants 2.2 and 10.2 and thicknesses 127 μm and 2.54 mm respectively.
The folded slot antenna provides better impedance matching and bandwidth compared to a simple slot.
The antenna patterns with EBG substrate show reduced cross-polarization levels and smoother main lobes.
The effective parallel-plate waveguide mode cutoff is controlled by the plate separation being less than half the guide wavelength.
The EBG structure can be modeled as an array of infinite dielectric rods excited by a TEM wave with axial electric field.
The measured antenna gain is higher than the theoretical directivity of a slot in infinite ground due to EBG reflection effects.
The study demonstrates the potential for low-profile, high-efficiency planar antennas using EBG substrates.
